title: The query engine: numbers from a person's own table, never their rows
request: The owner's goal: Home helps people who want data analysis, reports and business answers use DCLab's tools; H6 is the engine every such answer runs on.
spec: Package H6 of the Home plan: a versioned query plan, a validator, a pandas executor on the checked clean table, a row floor, an exposure log, a home_query purpose that sees column summaries only, with its data-limit test.
plan: Put the contract and its rules in dclab_core (query.py), the wiring in dclab_rnd (home_query.py).
Refuse every plan that could list rows; remove small groups and count them.
Reproduce the H1 analysis requests' answers with hand-written plans on the replica tables; review adversarially.

decisions.decision: An identifier is refused in every role (group, filter, measured value), only counted.
decisions.why: The review: filtering one id out of a total and subtracting revealed that person's value.

decisions.decision: A small group's minimum, maximum or extreme percentile is withheld.
decisions.why: In a group of five, the maximum is one person's own value; the row floor counts rows, not people.

decisions.decision: The table is read only against the hash recorded when it was prepared; a table without one is hashed on its first read.
decisions.why: An answer must come from the table the person prepared, never a file changed since.

change: dclab_core/query.py (QueryPlan v1, QueryResult v1, validate, execute, exposure); dclab_rnd/home_query.py (table, summaries, write_plan, run); prompts/home_query.md; purpose home_query; draft/pipeline.py records the clean table's hash; draft/orchestrator.py drops a stale one; .env.example DCLAB_ROW_FLOOR.

findings.defect: Whole-number amounts were taken for an identifier.
findings.scenario: A column of unique whole amounts was refused as a measure.
findings.cause: Numeric uniqueness alone made an identifier.
findings.fix: A number is an identifier only when its name says so.

findings.defect: An answer with no plan read as an empty plan.
findings.scenario: 'I cannot help' became a plan with no measure.

findings.defect: A committed module was overwritten by a new file of the same name.
findings.scenario: dclab_rnd/analysis.py (the research registry's evidence) was replaced by the new wiring.
findings.cause: The file's existence was not checked before writing.
findings.fix: Restored from git at once; the wiring is dclab_rnd/home_query.py.
findings.test: git diff of analysis.py is empty

findings.defect: Grouping by a customer id listed named customers' totals.
findings.scenario: 1,200 ids over 2,020 orders read as categorical; the answer named 28 customers.
findings.cause: Identifiers by uniqueness above 0.95 only, and the name rule for numbers only.
findings.fix: An id by its name or by more than half unique, for every type.

findings.defect: Subtracting two answers revealed one person's value.
findings.scenario: A total, and the same total filtered 'id ne E7', gave E7's exact salary.
findings.cause: Identifiers were refused only as groups.
findings.fix: Refused as filters, rate conditions and measured values too.

findings.defect: An inclusive end date dropped most of its last day.
findings.scenario: Hourly orders, end 2026-03-31: only the midnight row of that day was kept.
findings.cause: The comparison was with the day's first instant.
findings.fix: Up to the next day's start.

findings.defect: Malformed plans crashed or answered wrongly.
findings.scenario: A period on a region, 'amount gt abc', a one-value between, 'last quarter' as a date, a time-zoned column.
findings.cause: The validator did not check types, dates or the period column.
findings.fix: Each refused with its reason; any failure the validator missed becomes a refusal, never a crash.

findings.defect: A version draft carried a stale table hash and would be refused for ever.
findings.scenario: The version path copied the old hash, then rewrote the table.
findings.fix: Dropped there; a table without a hash is hashed on its first read.

findings.defect: A small group's maximum is one person's value.
findings.scenario: A group of five with max(salary).
findings.cause: The floor counts rows, not values.
findings.fix: Extremes withheld on groups under twice the floor.

measurements.name: The H1 analysis requests by hand-written plans on the replica tables
measurements.gate: the plan's done-when: each expected answer reproduced; no plan lists rows
measurements.result: Five requests reproduced exactly against pandas (revenue per region in a quarter, average order value by channel, orders per month, average spend by plan, share of customers above a ticket count per city); the missing-column request refused
limits: hand-written plans: the model writing plans is measured with the answers package
a difference of two allowed answers on ordinary categories can still narrow a small group; the floor is the guard

outcome: DCLab can answer a person's numeric question from their own checked table, refusing any plan that could list rows or single out a person.
lessons: A row floor counts rows, not people: identifiers and extremes need their own rules.
Check a file name is free before writing a new module.
risks: Differencing on ordinary categories can still narrow a group above the floor; H7 should log and limit repeated near-identical plans.
